newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN TELENET FINALISED GROUP STRUCTURE.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN TELENET FINALISED GROUP STRUCTURE.

text.p: Belgian Telenet, which plans to offer interactive services on the cable television network in Belgium's northern region of Flanders, said on Tuesday its group structure had been finalised.

Telenet said in a statement the upgrade of the cable network would cost 47 billion francs in the next 15 years, of which 37 billion would be paid by the Telenet partners, and 10 billion by the cable companies directly.

Telenet reiterated its plans to offer its first services in the autumn of 1997. Later it also plans to offer telephone services over the network in direct competition with national phone operator Belgacom.
The group said its partners had paid up 25 percent of Telenet Holding NV's 13 billion franc capital.

GIMV, the Flemish regional government's investment company, has a 20 percent stake; U.S. West International owns 25 percent; the Flemish cable companies themselves own 35 percent and a consortium of Flemish financial groups has the remaining 20 percent.

Telenet Holding controls Telenet Operations NV and Telenet Vlaanderen NV. Telenet Operations will invest in switching equipment and organise the operation of the network, while Telenet Vlaanderen will invest in the upgrade of local cable networks.
In Flanders 95 percent of homes is hooked up to cable TV distribution.
